featured_reviews.name: Paras
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shiv Sagar is a brand that everyone has heard off. They have close to 18 Outlets in Mumbai.

The best part about it is that the consistency in taste remained across all its outlets, that it what stands out. I still think that the Pav bhaji here is one of the best in Mumbai.

Nachos with Cheese Sauce
Crispy Nachos with cheese sauce which had a very thick consistency which defines how well the cheese sauce was. Goes well with bell peppers.
Rating - 8/10

Paneer Butter Masala
NOPE, not what you are expecting. It was a very crispy dosa with crumbled paneer inside it and it had the normal Mashed Potato stuffing in it. Trust me it was DIVINE. The Dosa was crispy throughout and I could literally taste the butter. The Sambar was also delicious with the Tomato Chutney. ORDER IT!
Rating - 10/10

Paneer Makhmali Tikka
Makhmali Tikka generally contains Salt pepper and curd marination, this one also had sugar in it. Which really made it too sweet to consume. You can miss out on this one.
Rating - 3/10

Idli Chilli
OMG the quantity is like WOW. Typical Chinese flavour that you would expect from a Paneer Chilli. Just instead of Paneer here it was Idli and it was Crispy as well.
Rating - 9/10

Cheese Kadai Pav Bhaji
I like the Pav Bhaji (PB) to be DOUBLE spicy and he happily made it for me. So being a Kadai PB I was expecting it to come in some Handi but it was Khada Pav bhaji with exact same taste from normal PB. It was AMAZING still I will prefer normal PB over Kadai PB.
Rating - 10/10

Dal Tadka
One word to describe it. PERFECT. Tonnes of Garlic dumped inside it, exactly how I wanted it to be reason being - Garlic is BAE.
Rating - 10/10

Veg Kofta
Big chunks of Kofta waiting to be eaten up inside a very thick gravy made from lots of cashew paste and many other spices. The gravy was really atasty along with the Kofta but the only thing is it was too thick.
Rating - 8/10
Moong Dal Halwa
NOPE, it was made long ago and microwaved and served to me.
Rating - 6/10

Honorable Mention from Beverage section

Shiv Sagar Special Lassi
GO FOR IT! One of the BEST lassis' in town.
Rating - 10/10

Overall Rating - 4.5/5

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.review_text: The food was delicious and well-prepared, which made our dining experience enjoyable initially. However, the service was disappointing. featured_reviews.name: Viraj Khedekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a weekend lunch at Millo. The restaurant is located in the Kamala Mills compound, so getting there is pretty easy.

The ambience is great. The restaurant is well maintained, clean and beautiful. The outdoor seating should probably be avoided during the monsoon. The tables are well spaced and the music is just the right volume so you don't need to shout to talk.
The service is quick and friendly. They will explain the menu and the contents of the dishes very well. They also accommodate dietary restrictions. They charge 10% as service fee.
The menu is fully vegetarian and expansive. They mainly cover Asian, Italian, and Mexican cuisines. We started with the comforting and tasty hot and sour mini soup. The Italian Tartine was tasty, the crostini were perfect to munch on. The Chilaquiles Filo Cups were a miss, the cups were nicely crisp but the guacamole was totally bland. The udon noodles were extremely tasty and were the second best item we tasted. Mind you, the noodles portion is large (for three, I'd guess). The kitchen seems to have nailed the Asian and Italian cuisine.

Overall, the experience was largely comforting. Definitely recommended, would revisit to taste more of the large menu.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay S Vardekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Radhe Shyam Hotel to order food for takeaway, and the entire experience was disappointing.

When I first went to the counter to place my order, I was told to go to another counter because takeaway orders were handled there. At that counter, there wasn't even a proper menu available. Instead, I was handed a photocopied menu, which felt quite unprofessional.

After deciding what to order, I was then told to go back to the first counter to make the payment. At that point, I genuinely felt like I was playing "counter to counter" instead of ordering food.

After paying, I waited for about 10 minutes and asked about the status of my order. The staff member simply said, "Sir, time lagega," which was fine. However, he then told me, "Aap bahar khade raho" in a rude and arrogant manner. He repeated this twice, which made me feel unwelcome as a customer.

Good food alone is not enough—customer service matters too. The lack of coordination, poor ordering process, and disrespectful attitude of the staff completely ruined the experience for me.

I collected my order and left, but unfortunately, I won't be visiting this place again.

After reading some of the other reviews, I guess I should consider myself lucky that the food turned out to be good and safe to eat. That's the only reason I'm giving this place an extra star. Otherwise, based on the service experience alone, it would have been a 1-star review.

featured_reviews.name: 1sh Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: The sheer variety on the thali is overwhelming in the best way possible. I loved how they balanced the sweet Gujarati flavors with the spicy Rajasthani dishes. We also tried the Shojo, which added a refreshing and slightly lighter touch to the otherwise intense flavor profile of the dishes.

To end on a sweet note, we ordered the Mathilda Cakes Pull Me Up. It was a delightful dessert that offered a decadent and fun experience, perfectly capping off our evening.

Overall, Yazu delivered a memorable culinary experience with a well-rounded menu and elegant atmosphere. It's a great choice for those looking to explore Pan Asian cuisine with a modern twist in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazu is a Pan‑Asian “supper club” concept that brings together flavors from Japan, China, Thailand, Korea and Southeast Asia under one roof. The Lower Parel outlet is positioned as a flagship. The place is spacious combining indoor and outdoor elements. The branding emphasizes “visual experiences” — sculptural ceiling installations, patterned concrete flooring, carved wooden walls, lighting as focal décor elements. Ambience is amazing: stylish, atmospheric, good for evenings, date nights, or a premium outing. The décor and lighting get special and the ceiling installation, carved walls, and an aesthetic that’s “Instagram‑worthy.” After sundown, it transforms into a high‑energy bar/music venue  like “Studio Nights”.
Wide and ambitious menu: sushi, sashimi, maki, dim sum, baos (Taiwanese street bun), Teppanyaki, Robata grill items, curries, fusion dishes (e.g. “Asian Pizza‑San”) etc. They offer special dietary menus: Jain and Keto options. Go for signature dishes (e.g. sushi rolls, baos, dim sum) early; save room for dessert.
Top Picks:
• Black crispy Asparagus Roll (sushi) • Steamed Veg. Cheung Fung • Veg. Dimsum Experience Basket (7 piece) • Spicy Lotus root • Mah Poh Tofu etc.
• For soups: the Tom Kha, Tom Yum are superb.
• Desserts are also a highlight: “Pull Me Up Tiramisu”, “Berry Blossom Cheesecake”, “Salted Caramel Tart”, Coconut Panna Cotta etc. Presentation is premium, textures and flavors seem well balanced in many reviews.
• Drinks are highly inventive, globally inspired, and expertly crafted. Every sip is bold and gives unforgettable experience. Loved its Samurai (cocktail), Shojo and Yashi (mocktails) which were flavorful and refreshing.
Attentive and polite staff who guide through the menu, make recommendations, and ensure a comfortable dining experience. Yazu Lower Parel is a strong pick if you're looking for a premium Pan‑Asian dining + bar experience in Mumbai. The ambience, décor, and overall concept are standout features. The place has a premium, elegant vibe and delivers a memorable night out.

Celebrating Wins, the Bhagat Tarachand Way

After a quick visit to Siddhivinayak to celebrate a friend’s professional milestone, we were in the mood for some solid vegetarian food. Naturally, Bhagat Tarachand came to mind. With so many versions out there, we just went with the closest—Bhagat Tarachand B. And it turned out to be a fantastic choice.

They offer valet parking, which is always a plus in the city. Surprisingly, even on a Monday night, there was a 40-minute wait. That said, their waiting area is well set up—plush sofas inside, extra seating outside, and the vibe inside is vibrant and upscale. Yes, a bit noisy, but still cozy. The staff was courteous, attentive, and knew their menu well.

What We Ordered:
•	Papad Churi: A classic, and they nailed it.
•	Pav Bhaji: Flavorful, though slightly on the sweeter side for my taste.
•	Shev Tamatar Sabji: Outstanding. Comfort food at its best.
•	Veg Dehati: We were torn between this and Veg Chili Mili. The waiter recommended Dehati, and he was spot on—spicy, rich, and deeply satisfying.

To go with it:
•	Special Ghee Roti: Soft and comforting.
•	Missi Roti & Makai Roti: These missed the mark for us. Definitely had better versions elsewhere.

Final Verdict:

Despite a couple of misses, Bhagat Tarachand B lives up to its reputation. The food was rich, flavorful, and satisfying. If you’re looking for elevated vegetarian dining with a touch of tradition, it’s definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited SpiceKlub to explore their newly launched menu, and it was truly an impressive experience for anyone who enjoys modern Indian fusion cuisine.
We started with their appetizers, and the Masala Pav Bagel Bites were an absolute highlight. It’s a creative take on Mumbai’s classic masala pav, served inside sesame bagels with a perfect balance of spiced onion-tomato masala, buttery chutney, and cream cheese. The flavours felt familiar yet completely elevated.
The Desi Hummus Dip was another standout dish. Unlike regular hummus, this one blends creamy chickpea hummus with bold, smoky Pindi chole flavours. The crunchy toppings and spiced oil drizzle added great texture and depth, making it a must-try for fusion lovers.
For beverages, we tried the Jamun Sour and Kanji Martini. The Jamun Sour was refreshing, tangy, and well-balanced with a hint of citrus, while the Kanji Martini offered a unique fermented flavour with mustard and kala namak notes — definitely something different and worth experiencing.
In the main course, the Hyderabadi Chilli Roast was beautifully executed. Stuffed green chillies filled with herbed goat cheese paired perfectly with the rich peanut, sesame, and coconut-based salan, offering a great balance of spice and creaminess.
The most unique part of the experience was the Bubbling Kulfi. It’s served at an extreme temperature and cannot be eaten directly, making it an interactive dessert where you mix it with add-ons before enjoying. A fun and innovative concept that stands out.
Overall, SpiceKlub truly delivers when it comes to creativity, presentation, and flavour. It’s the perfect place for anyone looking to try something different from the usual dining options in Mumbai. Highly recommended for fusion food lovers!

We absolutely love trying Fusion & Multicuisine Restaurants as we get to try Creative Dishes made from the Most Basic Ingredients! ❤️

We were recently at @gupshupinmumbai and had a Pleasant Experience.

Y’all must try their : Falafel & Hummus, Pudina Paneer Tikka ( Best ) , Palak Paneer, Mudcake ( Soo Good ) & Virgin Mojito! ❤️

📍Location : Gupshup ( Redefining Food ) , Unit no 5, Ground Floor, Building No 24, 11/12, Raghuvanshi Mills Compound, Senapati Bapat Marg, Lower Parel, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400013

featured_reviews.name: Sachi Gandhhi
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here for dinner a few days back but was not fully satisfied with the meal. We ordered the special pav Bhaji which tasted ok but the Bhaji was very less and the portion was way too small. I also ordered the avocado pani puri but the flavours were not going together very well and the avocado did not taste fresh. One dish which was really good was the falafel. Although we called for jain it was still tasty and flavourful. We also ordered the Mexican vadapav which was super cheesy and didn’t have much other Mexican flavours. Another dish we ordered was the Maggi balls which tasted good but were little dry. All the food we ordered was average so was a good meal but don’t think I would visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Chanchal Rathi
featured_reviews.review_text: I tried this interesting named restaurant and the food was so good! Manchurian cheese wrap was juicy and quite flavorful! The interesting order was fried Maggi balls. They taste nothing like Maggi but they are quite good! The portion size and taste of schezwan noodles was quite amazing! I also had the dal makhni! The dal was a perfect thing to go with my home cooked rice! Overall, amazing portion size and food!

featured_reviews.name: jinal panchal
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Hanging with friends out we were hungry and in search of good place around and found Gupshup Redefining Food that is in lower parel West, near Senapati Bapat Marg Road.

Ambience of the place is super beautiful loved it, the lighting of the place is bright and makes toh feel awesome.

In food we started with mocktails i.e Strawberry Mojito that was very refreshing
In starters we had Mexican Pani Puri and Black pizza ...Pani Puri was with cheese and pizza was amazing with cheese veggies and olives.

In mains we ordered Paneer Tikka Masala with Whole Wheat Roti and Gupshup Biryani and it was loaded with the textures of masala and was amazing.

In dessert we had brownie tutti fruity sundae that was Soo yumm.The food and serving was super good had a great time.

featured_reviews.name: Ajay Chaudhari
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gupshup at Lower Parel, is great place to dine out. I personally loved the place. The place has a great Ambiance. My family enjoyed the place as well. I personally loved the Paneer Shezwan Cheese Roll.
We had Paneer Handi and Naan for the Breakfast, which were delicious too. If you're a Biryani lover, you should definitely try the Gupshup Biryani. The star of the show were the desserts. We had Brownie Tutti Fruity Sundae, which was greattt.
I really loved the venue and would love to give t another visit

featured_reviews.name: Palak Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Raghuvanshi Mills

Sad / bad quality of food and service.
Dingy entrance and a bad foul smell in the restaurant.
When you pay high prices for street food, you expect something slightly different from the usual, but this is a loot !
A really bad experience.
Not recommended at all.

featured_reviews.name: Sakshi Andhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
GupShup- Redefining Food, if you are looking for best vegetarian outlet nearby lower parel then this is the place where you will get Vegetarian Meal. They serves Fast Food, Chaat, Variety of Dosa, South Indian food, Paav Bhaji etc. They have small but decent ambience you can dine in with your family and friends.

As per Name of the outlet we had GupShup Special Cutlets filled with veggies, even beautifully presented. Next we had Tandoori mushrooms and Cheese Corn balls with dip mayo, balls stuffed with cheese and corn. Along with this we had Mocktails GupShup special Mocktail and virgin mojito.

Talking about mains we had Jini Dosa, the most eye appealing presentation chutney served in two backets, it taste really amazing. Paav bhaji platter including Masala Paav, Bhaji, Salad, Onion, Lemon for taste. In dessert I had Brownie Tutti Fruity Sundae which was Just Amazing, I personally Liked It.

The best option for all Veg lovers. Do visit and enjoy GupShup!

featured_reviews.name: mayuresh m
featured_reviews.review_text: Great ambiance and fantastic vegetarian treats at Shrinathji. The food is flavorful, the atmosphere is welcoming, and the overall experience is very enjoyable. A great choice for veg food lovers!

featured_reviews.name: Aatmi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shreenathji’s is a vegetarian and Jain restaurant that offers a cozy, family-friendly ambiance. Their menu features a wide variety of dishes, including burgers, pizzas, sizzlers, salads, soups, pasta, starters, nachos, avocado bruschetta and fondue.

The Pav Bhaji Fondue was amazing—served hot with a creamy, tangy, and perfectly spiced taste that pairs beautifully with its accompaniments. The ‘Chinese water chestnut’ was something completely new yet definitely worth a try. The falafel was also well-prepared served alongside two condiments.

The Shrinathji Special Sizzler was great, offering bold and perfectly cooked flavors. Capsicum rings were nice, but personally, I didn’t prefer the crispy coating.

The classic sizzling brownie is the perfect way to end your meal🤤
